A 60+ person who cannot prepare her own meals can be a separate household only if the others' income is ≤ 165% FPL (about $2,976/mo for 2), which $5,500 exceeds. A tool counting only the parent's income would wrongly say yes.
programs.keyRule: 7 CFR 273.1(a)(2)(ii): separate household for an elderly person unable to purchase/prepare meals only if others' income ≤ 165% FPL

programs.name: Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program
alsoKnownAs: EHEAP (Emergency Home Energy Assistance for the Elderly, crisis only)
programs.agency: FloridaCommerce through Miami-Dade Community Action and Human Services Department
programs.reason: LIHEAP counts the whole household; the 3-person household's ~$6,900/mo is above the ~$4,329/mo limit.
programs.keyRule: Household income ≤ 60% of Florida state median income or 150% FPL (published table: $2,680/mo for 1, $3,504 for 2, $4,329 for 3; 2025 table)

programs.name: Florida homestead exemption plus Miami-Dade senior (65+) limited-income additional exemption
programs.agency: Miami-Dade County Property Appraiser
programs.reason: She lives in her daughter's home, so there is no homestead of her own; the daughter (58) is not 65+.
programs.keyRule: Homestead owner 65+ with 2025 household adjusted gross income ≤ $38,686 gets an additional exemption (up to $50,000 off county/participating-city taxes) for 2026

programs.name: Optional State Supplementation
programs.agency: Florida DCF
programs.reason: OSS only pays for people living in a licensed assisted living facility, adult family care home or mental health residential facility; she lives at home.
programs.keyRule: Must reside in an ALF, AFCH or MHRTF

firstCall.program: VA Survivors Pension with Aid and Attendance
firstCall.phoneOrWhere: Miami-Dade County Veteran Services Program, 305-756-2830 (Hialeah Community Resource Center, 305-884-4801, Wed/Fri)
firstCall.why: She clearly qualifies now with no waitlist or spend-down, and the monthly cash can pay for help that relieves the daughter. The ADRC call (305-670-4357) for SMMC LTC/HCE screening should follow, since a spend-down plan for the $9,000 has to be coordinated with both programs.

families.notes: Confirm whether the 'small widow's pension' is already a VA Survivors Pension or DIC; if basic pension, request the A&A increase; DIC and pension cannot both be paid. Payments to the daughter for care under a written agreement may count as medical expenses for VA. SMMC LTC's participant-directed option can pay a non-spouse family caregiver such as the daughter. Spend-down must avoid gifts (Medicaid 5-year look-back; VA 3-year).
